headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads/writes only its own account-file workflow and files like videos/demo.mp4, while Agent B can read/write the filesystem and process stdin/stdout. A shared workspace or copied outputs would let B ingest A-produced content as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and not higher.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or copied outputs are fed from A to B, injection becomes reachable.
IF B parses A-generated text or files as instructions without provenance checks, malicious content can steer B.
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent.
Disable automatic parsing of A outputs by B.
Add a provenance header and reject untrusted instruction blocks.
Review any copied files before B consumes them.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches account data and media files, and Agent B has broad filesystem read plus broad network egress. If they share a workspace, B can read A's local artifacts and transmit them externally. There is no evidence of a shared workspace by default, so the risk is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or mounted workspace, B can access A's files.
IF B is allowed to send retrieved files over the network, local account data can leave the host.
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers.
Mount A's workspace read-only for B, or not at all.
Block B's outbound network during file review.
Move sensitive account files out of shared paths.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A does not write the filesystem, but Agent B does. If both are given the same mutable directory, B's writes can overwrite A's media/account artifacts and create race conditions. Because A's session scope maps one account name to one account file, concurrent instances raise collision risk; uncertainty keeps this at high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory, B can clobber A's files.
IF multiple instances run concurrently on the same account name, account-file collisions can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Serialize access to shared account files.
Use file locks around any shared mutable path.
Run only one instance per account name.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes or lock coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can produce upload artifacts and account-related outputs, while Agent B can read files and act through pipelines or scripts. If B treats A's outputs as authoritative, A's mistakes or malicious content can cascade into B's downstream actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF B consumes A's outputs without validation, incorrect metadata or prompts can propagate.
IF B is configured to execute scripts or pipeline steps from A-produced files, downstream actions can be wrong or unsafe.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Validate A outputs against a schema before B uses them.
Reject executable content from A.
Log and diff A outputs before downstream use.
requires-engineering: add typed interfaces between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles account data and social-media media, while Agent B handles multimodal data and has broad network egress. If account data includes regulated personal content and B processes or uploads it, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so this is a compliance-gap inference, not a direct violation.
conditions: IF account data includes personal data subject to retention or residency rules, B's processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF B stores or forwards A's media beyond the intended jurisdiction, compliance obligations can be breached.
mitigations: Classify the data before sharing it with B.
Keep regulated data out of B's inputs.
Set explicit retention limits for B's outputs.
Restrict B's network destinations.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
